title: 1:1 Siddartha and Aditya
overview: Siddartha and Aditya discussed Aditya's workload, which has grown because of the on-call rotation, and agreed to move on-call to a shared weekly rotation among four people. They talked about the path to a senior engineer role, where the gap is owning decisions across teams rather than technical depth, and agreed Aditya will lead the design of the PDF service. Aditya also asked to attend a distributed systems workshop in Bengaluru next month.

chapters.title: Workload and on-call
bullets: Aditya has carried the on-call week twice in the last month and is tired
Agreed to move on-call to a weekly rotation across four people
Aditya wants fewer interruptions during the days he is working on design

chapters.title: Growth towards senior engineer
bullets: Technical depth is already at the senior level
The gap is owning decisions that affect other teams and writing them down
Aditya will lead the design of the PDF service and present it to the team

chapters.title: Mentoring and learning
bullets: Aditya will pair with Saloni for an hour a week on API design
He wants to attend a two day distributed systems workshop in Bengaluru next month
Siddartha will approve the budget once the cost is confirmed

action_items.text: Set up the new four person on-call rotation starting next week
Write the design document for the PDF service and present it to the team
Share the details and cost of the distributed systems workshop
Approve the workshop budget and confirm leave dates
Pair with Saloni for an hour each week on API design

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: Hey Aditya. Thanks for making time, I know sprint planning ran long this week. Let me start with an open question. How are you doing, really?

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: I'm okay. Honestly, a little tired. The last month was heavy. I was on call twice, and the incident last week meant a few late nights.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: Yeah, I was worried about that. I looked at the rota and you did two out of the last four weeks. That's not fair, and I should have caught it earlier.

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: It's not only the rota. It's that when I'm on call, I also get pinged for things that aren't on-call. People know I fix things quickly, so they come to me.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: That's a good problem to have for your reputation, and a bad problem for your calendar. What would help?

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: A proper rotation, honestly. Weekly, and with more than just me and Karthik. Saloni and you could also be in it.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: Me as well, yes. It's good for me to feel the pain. Let's make it a four person rotation, starting next week, one week each. I'll set it up and write down what counts as an escalation, so people stop pinging you directly for small things.

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: That would be a big relief. Thank you.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: Okay. Second thing. You asked last time about what it would take to get to senior engineer. I've thought about it properly, so let me be honest.

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: Please. I'd rather hear it straight.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: On the technical side, you're already there. The ingestion work, the retry logic, the incident fix, all of it is senior level. The gap is something different. It's owning decisions that cross team boundaries, and writing them down so that others can understand why.

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: Can you give me an example?

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: The speaker clean-up. You fixed it in three days, which was great. But the original choice was made without anyone else seeing it. A short design note, shared before you built it, would have let Karthik ask the question about long transcripts.

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: That's fair. I tend to just build it when I know how.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: Which is a good instinct for speed. For senior, I want you to also use that instinct to bring others along. Here's what I'd suggest. The PDF service is coming up. Lead the design, write a two page document, and present it to the team before you start. I'll review it with you.
comments: Use the design note template from the incident review. It already has the 'what if this is ten times bigger' section.

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: I like that. I've never presented a design to the whole team before. A bit nervous, to be honest.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: That's normal. We'll practise together once before, and Harshita will ask the product questions, so you won't be alone.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: One more on growth. Saloni mentioned she'd like to learn more about backend work. Would you be open to pairing for an hour a week?

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: Yes, definitely. She's sharp. I could also learn from the frontend side, since I never know how my API looks to the person using it.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: Perfect. That's a good exchange. Can you start next week?

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: Yes. Let's say Wednesday afternoons. Actually, can I ask about a workshop? There's a two day course on distributed systems in Bengaluru next month. It's run by people from a few of the larger product companies, and it's mostly about consistency and queues, which is exactly what we've been dealing with.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: What does it cost?

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: I think around thirty-five thousand rupees, plus travel. I'll send you the exact details.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: That's fine, we have a learning budget and you haven't used yours this year. Send me the dates, so I can check they don't clash with the freeze. And after you come back, I'd like you to give a thirty minute talk to the team on what you learned.

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: Of course. That's a fair deal.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: Okay, anything else on your mind? Anything about the team, or me?

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: Just one thing. The Thursday check-ins have been useful. Please keep them. It helps when the whole team knows what's happening.

segments.speaker: Siddartha Nepal
segments.text: I will. Thanks, Aditya. And thanks for being honest about the workload. Please tell me earlier next time, don't wait for a one on one.

segments.speaker: Aditya Verma
segments.text: I will. Thank you.
